title: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The constraint in the minimum-enclosing-hypersphere problem is written as u_i^j o_i^T <= R_i (inner product of each point with the center). This does NOT enforce that points lie inside the sphere. The correct formulation is ||u_i^j - o_i|| <= R_i (or ||u_i^j - o_i||^2 <= R_i^2). Counterexample: for points u^1=(10,0), u^2=(0,0), the printed constraint admits the 'solution' o=(0,0), R=0 (both inner products are 0 <= 0), yet u^1 is at distance 10 from the center - clearly not encapsulated. The printed program is a linear program in the projection width, not a hypersphere enclosure.

The reported RSum for the 'w/o L_div' ablation is 191.7, but the three components sum as 35.1 + 69.4 + 84.1 = 188.6. The arithmetic is internally inconsistent (off by 3.1), indicating an erroneous RSum value or a component entry in this row.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 vs Table 2, RoMa baseline rows
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: RoMa is reported with different numbers in the two tables for the same method/dataset/protocol. Table 1 (coarse): ScanRefer 11.4/34.8/54.4/100.6, Nr3D 6.5/24.8/37.6/68.9. Table 2 (base row): ScanRefer 9.7/33.1/50.2/93.0, Nr3D 8.3/27.9/37.2/73.4. The other two baselines that appear in both tables (VSEinf and CRCL) are IDENTICAL across tables, so the discrepancy is specific to RoMa. In particular Table 2's RoMa ScanRefer triple (9.7/33.1/50.2) is exactly VSEinf's values, strongly suggesting a copy-paste error.

The text states 'we introduce eleven comparative baseline methods', but then enumerates five conventional (VSEinf, CHAN, HREM, CRCL, RoMa) + three interactive (ChatIR, Rewrite, MERLIN) + two additional strong interactive baselines (IR, SUM) = 5+3+2 = 10 methods. Table 1 also lists exactly 10 baseline rows. The count 'eleven' is inconsistent with the enumeration and the table.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2.1, Adaptive Questioning (density bias claim), reference [60]
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The in-text citation '[60] Zhang, L., Wang, M., & Liu, Q. (2022). Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval. In Proceedings of ICLR 2022.' is invoked as the theoretical foundation for Bayesian density correction. Web searches for the exact title/authors returned no record of such a paper at ICLR 2022 or elsewhere. Additionally, the reference list of this paper only contains entries [1]-[59], so [60] is absent from the bibliography and appears only as an inline APA-style entry in the body - consistent with a hallucinated citation.

The opening argument sentence is truncated: 'Although existing dedicated methods [6] achieve promising performance for T3SR by facilitating fine-grained query text and scene understanding, such success often relies on the assumption that' - the sentence is never completed before the text jumps to the conference header '39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)' and Figure 1. The core motivating claim of the Introduction is left dangling.

The section contains a dangling fragment 'We then simulate the' followed by a blank line and a restatement 'We simulate the IRR interaction process by iteratively posing a fixed number of Q1 and Q2 questions.' The first attempt at this sentence is truncated mid-clause, leaving broken text in the method description.

The Abstract claims IDeal 'completely solves the alignment challenge between texts and 3D scenes through continuous interaction, achieving near-perfect retrieval accuracy across diverse query types'. The Limitations paragraph states 'the performance of the methods is relatively low', and Section 4.5 states performance 'lacks a robust automatic stopping criterion, limiting its practical applicability'. With best reported R@1 of only 37.8 (ScanRefer, fine-grained) and 12.8 (coarse), 'near-perfect retrieval accuracy' is contradicted by the paper's own results and limitations.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 vs Table 2, IDeal-dagger Nr3D row
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The fine-grained 'IDeal-dagger' configuration on Nr3D is reported as 26.4/62.7/78.7/167.8 in Table 1 but as 25.4/60.7/75.7/161.8 in Table 2 (RoMa + IDeal-dagger row), while the ScanRefer rows for the same named configurations are numerically identical (37.8/71.8/86.4/196.0) across both tables. Two tables cannot simultaneously agree on ScanRefer and disagree on Nr3D for the same configuration without an error in one of them.

Section 4.5 claims 'Interaction improves performance up to an optimal number of rounds (approximately five rounds with fine-grained and three rounds with coarse-grained descriptions), after which performance plateaus or degrades by up to 2-3% R@1'. The tabulated Figure 4 data for fine-grained memory (ScanRefer purple: 20,27,30,35,37,39,40,40 over rounds 0-7) shows monotonic improvement up to round 6-7 with no degradation at round 5 (39, still rising), so the 'five rounds optimal, then degrades 2-3%' claim is not supported by the figure's own data for the fine-grained case.

summary: The paper proposes IDeal for interactive text-3D scene retrieval (IRR framework + IAT adaptation). Exhaustive verification (lenient strictness) found 10 issues. The most serious: (1) Equation (4) states the minimum-enclosing-hypersphere constraint as u_i^j o_i^T <= R_i, which mathematically does not enclose the points (correct form is ||u_i^j - o_i|| <= R_i) - an erratum-worthy displayed-equation error; (2) Table 3 'w/o L_div' row reports RSum 191.7 while its components sum to 188.6; (3) the RoMa baseline is reported with conflicting values in Table 1 vs Table 2, with the Table 2 ScanRefer row exactly duplicating VSEinf's values, suggesting a copy-paste error; (4) the text claims 'eleven' baselines but enumerates ten; (5) reference [60] ('Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval', ICLR 2022) has no web trace and is missing from the reference list, consistent with a fabricated citation. Additional moderate issues include truncated/dangling sentences in the Introduction, Section 3.3 and Section 4.4, an abstract overclaim ('completely solves / near-perfect retrieval accuracy') that conflicts with the paper's stated limitations and low absolute R@1, a missing 'Case 3' in the Figure 5 caption/body, and a Figure 4 text-claim/data mismatch on the optimal number of interaction rounds. Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION.
